# How to read a range

::: {.callout-note}
Revised with assistance from OpenAI Codex/GPT-6. Earlier skeleton drafted by Claude Code/Fable 5.1. This summary remains unfinished.
:::

Children of the same age can have different vocabulary counts. The middle estimate describes the centre of a predictive distribution. The range describes possible observed counts under the model, including variation between children and between assessments.

A 50% predictive interval contains at least half the model's probability for a possible count. It does not promise that half of children in every classroom will fall inside it. A probability of one in 20 means 5% under the stated model and conditions.

An interval around the reference curve describes uncertainty about that curve. It can be narrow even when the range of possible counts for a new child is wide. Use the predictive range when discussing a possible assessment.
